content: The screen is flashing or has become dark 1. If your TV is flickering or dimming sporadically, you may need to disable some of the energy efficiency features. 2. Disable Brightness Optimisation, Energy Saving Solution, Motion Lighting or Contrast Enhancer. 3. Settings > All Settings > General & Privacy > Power and Energy Saving > Brightness Optimisation 4. Settings > All Settings > General & Privacy > Power and Energy Saving > Energy Saving Solution 5. Settings > All Settings > General & Privacy > Power and Energy Saving > Motion Lighting 6. Settings > All Settings > Picture > Expert Settings > Contrast Enhancer 7. Some OLED models automatically decrease the screen brightness when the ambient temperature is high, to prevent afterimages. 8. Run Picture Test. When the tested image quality is normal, check the signal of the connected device. 9. Settings > Support > Device Care > Self Diagnosis > Picture Test

content: The picture colours are black and white or do not look the way they should look 1. If the product's colours or absolute whites/blacks seem to be off, launch Picture Test. 2. Settings > Support > Device Care > Self Diagnosis > Picture Test 3. If the test results indicate that the problem is not caused by the TV, do the following: 4. When using the One Connect Box, confirm that its video input connectors are connected to the correct external device video output connectors. 5. If using a component cable, ensure that the green (Y), blue (Pb), and red (Pr) cables are connected properly. Incorrect connections may cause colour problems or a blank screen. 6. Component port may not be supported depending on the model. 7. Check whether Greyscale is set to On. 8. Settings > All Settings > General & Privacy > Accessibility > Greyscale

content: The TV automatically turns off by itself 1. If your TV appears to turn off by itself, try disabling some of the TV's energy efficiency functions. 2. See if Sleep Timer has been enabled. The Sleep Timer automatically turns the TV off after a specified period of time. 3. Settings > All Settings > General & Privacy > Power and Energy Saving > Sleep Timer 4. If the Sleep Timer has not been enabled, see if Auto Power Off or Off Timer has been enabled and disable it. 5. Settings > All Settings > General & Privacy > Power and Energy Saving > Auto Power Off 6. Settings > All Settings > General & Privacy > Power and Energy Saving > Off Timer

content: TV cannot be turned off. 1. On some models, you can turn off the TV by pressing and holding the Power button. To switch from Art mode to TV mode or vice versa, short-press the Power button when the TV is on. 2. Configure operation settings for the power button on the remote control in Settings > All Settings > General & Privacy > Remote Control > Power Button Option. This feature is set to Art/TV by default. 3. If you briefly press the power button on the remote control, switches to Art mode or TV mode. If you set this feature to On/Off, the TV turns on or off. 4. This function may not be supported depending on the model.

3. If you briefly press the power button on the remote control, switches to Art mode or TV mode. If you set this feature to On/Off, the TV turns on or off.

content: Unable to power on 1. If you are having problems powering on your TV, there are a number of things to check before calling the service department. 2. Confirm that the TV's power cord is connected correctly at both ends and that the remote control is operating normally. 3. Make sure that the antenna cable or cable TV cable is firmly connected. 4. If you have a cable box or satellite box, confirm that it is plugged in and turned on. 5. If your TV model supports the One Connect Box, check the One Connect Cable connecting the TV to the One Connect Box or check the connection between the TV and One Connect Box.

content: The TV remains on or does not turn on automatically. 1. If the surrounding area is too dark or bright, the motion sensor may not work normally. The performance of the motion sensor may be affected by the installation environment (height, tilt, obstacles). If the clothes you wear or your skin colour is similar to the surrounding shading, the motion sensor may not work properly. 2. Motion Sensor may not be supported depending on the model or geographical area. 3. The TV responds to all visual changes around it (lights, displays, dogs, out-of-window changes and other occurrences). You can adjust the response level by adjusting the sensitivity of the motion detector. 4. (top of Smart Hub Home screen) Art > Art Options > Sleep Options > Motion Detector 5. Art Options can be found at the bottom of the Art home. To configure the option settings, scroll down to the far bottom. 6. Motion Detector may not be supported depending on the model or geographical area.

content: The TV image does not look as good as it did in the store. 1. Store displays are tuned to a digital UHD channel or HD channel. 2. Change the output resolution of your devices such as digital broadcast receiver, IPTV and set-top box to UHD or HD. 3. Be sure to use an HDMI cable to enjoy high quality videos. 4. Connected Devices > Connection Guide > Video Device > HDMI 5. To connect the TV with your PC, make sure that your PC's graphic card supports UHD resolutions. 6. Make sure that the set-top box or cable box supports the content or broadcast for UHD and set the resolution. For more information, contact your service provider. 7. When using a Samsung TV Plus channel, check the network connection. When the network speed is slow, the app may not work or the image quality may be poor.

content: The picture is distorted. 1. The compression of video content may cause picture distortions, especially in fast moving pictures from sports programmes and action movies. 2. Remove and reconnect the power cord, and check the remote control battery. 3. If the signal reception is weak or poor, screen distortion may be visible but it is not a malfunction. 4. Mobile phones used close to the TV (within 1 m) may cause noise on analogue or digital channels. 5. This function may not be supported depending on the model or geographical area.

Check the volume control of your TV, and then check the volume control of the external device (cable box or satellite box, DVD, Blu-ray, etc.) connected to your TV. 2. Check the cable connection between an external device and the TV, and then try cable connection again.

content: The picture is good but there is no sound. 1. Check the Sound Output setting. If it is set to TV Speaker, check the volume setting. 2. Settings > All Settings > Sound > Sound Output 3. If you are using an external device, check the device’s audio output option. 4. For example, you may need to change your cable box’s audio option to HDMI if the box connected to your TV is using an HDMI cable. 5. To listen to computer sound, connect an external speaker to the computer’s audio output connector. 6. If your TV has a headphone jack, make sure there is nothing plugged into it. 7. Reboot the connected device by disconnecting and then reconnecting the device’s power cord. 8. With a set-top box or cable box, check the cable connection and reboot the external device. When the symptom persists, contact your service provider.

metadata.symptom: The picture is good but there is no sound.

2. Settings > All Settings > Sound > Sound Output
3. If you are using an external device, check the device’s audio output option.
4. For example, you may need to change your cable box’s audio option to HDMI if the box connected to your TV is using an HDMI cable.
5. To listen to computer sound, connect an external speaker to the computer’s audio output connector.
6. If your TV has a headphone jack, make sure there is nothing plugged into it.
7. Reboot the connected device by disconnecting and then reconnecting the device’s power cord.
8. With a set-top box or cable box, check the cable connection and reboot the external device. When the symptom persists, contact your service provider.

content: The sound is interrupted. 1. Sound quality may become affected if the wireless router is close to the Bluetooth speaker. Place the Bluetooth speaker as close as possible to the TV without obstacle between them. Do not place the wireless router close to the Bluetooth speaker body. 2. To minimise interruptions, we recommend a wireless access point that uses a 5 GHz or 6 GHz frequency. 5 GHz or 6 GHz may not be supported depending on the model. 3. When the symptom persists, it is recommended to use wired connection such as HDMI (eARC/ARC) and Optical.

content: Wireless network connection failed. Unable to connect to a wireless access point. Unable to connect to the network. 1. Settings > Support > Device Care > Self Diagnosis > Smart Hub Connection Test 2. Ensure that the network cable is connected and the router is powered on. 3. Connect your mobile device to the router via Wi-Fi. 4. Turn the router off and back on again. (Requires 2 to 3 minutes) 5. If a security key is required, make sure it has been entered correctly. 6. Unplug the TV’s power cord and plug it back in or press and hold the power button for at least 3 seconds. 7. Make sure that there is no electromagnetic wave generating device placed between the TV and router. 8. If unable to establish a wireless internet connection, connect the TV to the wireless router via a LAN cable. 9. If the TV is able to connect to the internet normally via the cable connection, there might be a problem with the wireless router. In this case, try using a different wireless router. 10. Wired networks are not supported by some models.

metadata.symptom: Wireless network connection failed. Unable to connect to a wireless access point. Unable to connect to the network.

2. Ensure that the network cable is connected and the router is powered on.
3. Connect your mobile device to the router via Wi-Fi.

5. If a security key is required, make sure it has been entered correctly.
6. Unplug the TV’s power cord and plug it back in or press and hold the power button for at least 3 seconds.
7. Make sure that there is no electromagnetic wave generating device placed between the TV and router.
8. If unable to establish a wireless internet connection, connect the TV to the wireless router via a LAN cable.
9. If the TV is able to connect to the internet normally via the cable connection, there might be a problem with the wireless router. In this case, try using a different wireless router.
10. Wired networks are not supported by some models.
